snapshot_warning: PHASE A SNAPSHOT, TAKEN WHILE A BATCH OF AGENTS IS PUSHING TO THIS REPOSITORY. This is a point-in-time record, not a deletion list. Do not act on it. Phase B (blocked on #578 and #588) must collect a fresh live observation with scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs and authorize every deletion against that observation, not against this file -- deletionAuthorizationFindings refuses outright when no observation is supplied. The previous version of this fixture is the proof that snapshots go stale: it recorded seven heads, three of which had been merged and auto-deleted before the next snapshot was taken, while three that did not exist then had appeared.
method: Read-only. Every external fact in this file came from scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs, which runs each command and records the command line, exit code, byte count and a SHA-256 of its raw stdout beside the answer; those receipts are in live_observation.receipts and the observation's own digest is in live_observation.digest. Branch heads were taken over two independent transports (`git ls-remote --heads origin` and the REST branch list) and cross-checked. Containment came from `git merge-base --is-ancestor` and `git rev-list --count` in both directions; release-tag containment from `git tag --contains`; the whole protection object, the rulesets, the repository settings and the open pull requests from the REST API; the install source from digests of .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json and the package identity. The reference scan is two receipted sweeps per branch: a GitHub-wide issue/PR search and a `git grep` over the whole tree excluding this audit's own files. No ref was created, deleted, renamed or force-pushed to produce this file; the one branch this work adds to origin is the branch it is submitted from, recorded in heads_created_after_this_snapshot.

live_observation.note: The receipts below let a reader with credentials re-run each command and compare digests. What they cannot do is prove the observation came from GitHub rather than from a text editor -- an offline checker cannot authenticate a transcript. That boundary is stated rather than hidden, and it is why Phase B's authorization takes a freshly collected observation as a parameter instead of reading this one.

invariant_baseline.note: The state Phase B must find unchanged after it deletes anything, recorded before any deletion. Protection and rulesets are stored as the complete objects the API returned, not a projection: three booleans out of twelve fields cannot report that a fourth changed, and two rulesets of equal length are not the same two rulesets.

revision_history.note: First snapshot (PR #592). Classified task/issue-588-mark-done as must_be_preserved because its PR-list query found no PR referencing it; PR #591 had in fact been opened five minutes earlier. The query was stale before the document was produced.
Correction within PR #592: moved task/issue-588-mark-done into the open-PR-head table and recorded seven branches the coordinator reported that were not yet on origin.

Full re-collection at schema v2 after the previous snapshot's seven heads turned over. Added the six-value classification, release-tag containment, superseding evidence, the reference scan, protection status and a named list of what could not be established.

Schema v3. The external facts are no longer the audit author's transcript: they come from scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs with per-command receipts, over two independent transports for the head list, and the destructive decision now takes a freshly collected observation as a parameter and refuses without one. The invariant baseline stores the complete protection objects, the ruleset contents and the stable plugin/install source rather than a three-boolean projection. The Phase B deletion log is no longer emitted here -- it is the blocked phase's output, and this file records only the contract it must satisfy.

unestablished.why_it_does_not_bear: Intent is a question about the past; data loss is a question about the present, and the present is fully established here. The tip is an ancestor of both origin/dev and origin/main, `git rev-list origin/dev..` and `git rev-list origin/main..` both return 0, and the commit is contained in seven release tags. There is no object on this ref that deleting the ref would remove from the repository, whatever it was created for.

branches.reason: The tip commit e75d232 is an ancestor of both origin/dev and origin/main; git rev-list returns 0 commits unique to the branch against either, and git tag --contains places the commit in v0.1.11 through v0.1.17. The branch never carried a commit of its own -- it points at the merge commit of PR #511 (the chore/back-merge-0.1.10 chain) and never advanced from it. The receipted GitHub-wide search and tree scan find no reference to it outside this audit, issue #572's own candidate list, and the previous audit's PR. Deleting it, once #578 and #588 have cleared and a fresh live observation still shows it at this commit with no PR open, removes a name and no content.

unestablished.fact: what the branch was used to read, and whether anything was ever committed to it and later discarded
unestablished.searched: The receipted GitHub-wide sweep, a receipted `git grep` over the tree, and `git log --all --grep='claude artifact'` over the full history: nothing names it outside this audit, #572 and #592. A remote branch has no reflog readable from a clone, so a commit pushed and then force-replaced before this audit would leave no trace any command here can reach.
unestablished.why_it_does_not_bear: The question is about objects that are not on the ref now. The ref as it stands is an ancestor of both origin/dev and origin/main with 0 unique commits against either, so deleting it removes no reachable object. An object already unreachable from this ref is not preserved by keeping the ref either, which is precisely why #572 routes evidence into committed fixtures and issue records rather than leaving it on a branch.

branches.reason: The tip commit 2d6392f is fully contained in both origin/dev and origin/main (0 commits unique against either) and in release tags v0.1.16 and v0.1.17; it is the merge commit of PR #538, the chore/back-merge-0.1.15 chain, and the branch never advanced past it. It is a tmp/* branch, which repository policy caps at seven days or task end; it is past that. The receipted searches find no reference outside this audit, issue #572 and the previous audit's PR.

lifecycle.note: The PR carrying this audit must not use a closing keyword for #572. It completes the read-only-audit phase; final-deletion is blocked on #578 and #588 and is the phase that produces the deletion log.

phase_b_contract.note: The Phase B output is `branch-deletion-log`, which the canonical execution plan reserves for the final-deletion phase. That phase is blocked on #578 and #588, so no deletion log is emitted by this PR -- an audit that shipped the blocked phase's artifact would be doing Phase B's work in Phase A. What is recorded here is the contract that artifact has to satisfy, which is Phase A's job.
phase_b_contract.prerequisite_authority: fixtures/execution-plan/github-state.json -- #578 and #588 must be closed there with close evidence. The deletion log does not get to clear its own prerequisites; scripts/branch-audit.mjs cross-checks its claims against that snapshot and treats a disagreement as a finding.

repository_policy.note: The branch policy this issue asks to be written down. Descriptive of the repository's current settings where a setting exists, prescriptive where none does.
rules: feature/, task/ and fix/ branches are deleted once their PR merges. delete_branch_on_merge is enabled, so this happens automatically; the two branches in this audit that were not removed are the two that never had a PR.
tmp/* branches live at most seven days or until their task ends, whichever comes first. No setting enforces this; it is checked by re-running this audit.
release/ and hotfix/ branches are deleted after the release ships and the back-merge into dev lands.
main and dev are protected: no deletion, no force push, enforced for admins. No repository rulesets are configured.

A branch is not an evidence archive. Anything worth keeping is moved into a commit, a committed fixture, a document or an issue record before the branch it lived on is deleted -- which is why this issue's Phase B is blocked on #578 and #588 rather than running now.
